greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all as we gather in His presence today.
penitential:

homily:
We often think of the saints as figures carved in marble—distant, stoic, and somehow immune to the tremors of human life. We imagine them standing on pedestals, looking toward a horizon we cannot see. But today, as we celebrate Saint Ignatius of Antioch, we are confronted with something much more raw. Ignatius was a bishop who knew that his life was not his own. He was a man who, as he traveled toward his martyrdom, wrote letters that pulsed with a desperate, beautiful hunger for Christ. He did not want to be a monument; he wanted to be bread. He wanted his life to be consumed by the love of God, to be ground down like wheat in the teeth of wild beasts so that he might become a pure offering for the Church. There is a terrifying, holy intimacy in that desire. It is the desire to be entirely, completely, and irrevocably given over to the One who first gave Himself to us.

Think of the image of the 'eyes of the heart' that St. Paul uses in our first reading today. He prays that the eyes of our hearts might be enlightened, that we might know the hope to which we are called. This is not a vision of the physical eyes. The physical eyes see the world as it is—they see the empty chair, the photograph on the mantle, the calendar marking the passage of months. But the eyes of the heart? They see something else. They see the 'surpassing greatness of his power' that worked in Christ, raising him from the dead. They see the reality that is hidden behind the veil of our sorrow. They are the eyes that look at a life—even a life that seems to end too soon—and see not a tragedy, but a mystery of grace. They see that every life, no matter how brief, is held within the 'fullness of the one who fills all things in every way.'

I want to talk to you about the ache of these four months. I know that for you, Alan and Thao, the world has felt different since June. The silence in the house is not just an absence of sound; it is a weight. You have walked through the corridors of your home and felt the ghost of his presence—the way Ben would have been working on his code, the way he would have been talking about the latest airline routes, the way he would have been sharing a joke with Ryan. That ache is not a sign of failure. It is not a sign that you have lost your way. It is the ache of love that has nowhere left to go on this earth, so it turns upward, toward the One who holds him now. It is the same ache that Ignatius felt as he looked toward his end. It is the ache of a heart that is being stretched so it can hold more of God.

There is a truth we must name today, a truth that is often buried under the debris of our own self-questioning. Sometimes, when we lose someone we love, we begin to play back the tapes of our lives. We wonder if we missed a sign, if we could have been more watchful, if we could have done something differently. I want to tell you, as clearly as I can: you are not to blame. Illness is not a punishment, and it is not a result of anything you did or failed to do. God does not send these things, and He certainly does not hold you accountable for the mysteries of a life that is beyond our control. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were his world. You were his comfort. You did not miss anything. You are not being accused by God. You are being invited to rest in Him. Let that burden of 'what if' fall away. It is a heavy stone, and it was never meant for you to carry.

Benjamin Vo was a boy who lived with a singular, beautiful focus. He was a boy who understood that the heart is meant to be an offering. Think of that moment when he offered his entire piggy bank to help his uncle. He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it, he didn't need to make a spectacle of it. The offer itself was the truth of his soul. It was a movement of pure, unadulterated love. It was a reflection of the very heart of Christ, who offered everything—not because He was forced, but because He was love itself. Ben lived that way. He lived with a curiosity that touched everything—from the cold, precise logic of cloud infrastructure to the soaring, imaginative dreams of 'con chim airlines.' He was a boy who understood that the world is a place to be explored, a place to be served, and a place to be loved.

And now, he is in the place where all those dreams find their fulfillment. When the Gospel tells us today that 'the Holy Spirit will teach you at that moment what you should say,' it is a promise that we are never left to navigate our grief alone. Even when we cannot find the words—even when our prayers are just sighs or tears—the Holy Spirit is there, translating our ache into the language of heaven. You are not praying into a vacuum. You are praying into the arms of the Father who knows Ben by name, who knows the exact shape of his smile, and who knows every single dream he ever had for 'con chim airlines.'

Ryan, you are a brother who knows this truth in your own way. You have walked this road alongside Ben, and you continue to walk it now. You are the one who carries the legacy of his kindness. When you feel the weight of his absence, remember that you are not just a brother who has lost a friend; you are a brother who is bonded to him in the Body of Christ. That bond is not broken by death. It is transformed. It is made eternal. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the brother who knows that the most important things in life are not the things we possess, but the love we share. You are a witness to the world that love is stronger than the grave.

I want you to think about the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam. That well is a perfect image of what Benjamin’s life has become. It is not a monument to a life that ended; it is a source of life that continues. It is a sign that his love is still flowing, still quenching the thirst of those in need, still bringing life to the dry places. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to hope in the face of despair, you are allowing his legacy to refresh the world. You are turning the soil of the earth so that the Kingdom can grow. You are the ones who are keeping his light burning in a world that so often forgets to look up.

There is a profound freedom in realizing that we do not have to hold it all together. We do not have to be the ones who provide the answers. We are children of the promise. We are heirs to a kingdom that is not built by human hands, but by the grace of God. That grace is the 'bread' we need for the journey. It is the strength that comes when our own strength is gone. It is the peace that settles over us when we finally stop fighting the silence and start listening to the voice of the Father.

So today, carry this away with you: you are never alone. You are a family that is being held by the same hands that hold the universe. When you see a bird in flight, or a plane climbing into the clouds, don't just see a machine or a creature; see a sign of the freedom that Benjamin now knows. See a sign of the promise that you are walking toward. Keep your eyes on the horizon. The journey is not over; it is simply continuing in a new, more glorious way. And one day, when the long road reaches the end, you will look up and see him waiting for you, and the joy will be beyond all reckoning.

Take this with you: you are a family of four, and that will never change. The geography of your life has shifted, but the bond of your love is eternal. Keep the 'Well of Love' flowing in his name. Keep the kindness moving. Keep the dream alive. And when you walk out those doors, look up at the sky. Remember that he is not in the dust. He is in the light. He is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the harvest is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may His face shine upon you and give you peace. Go in the peace of Christ.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben, and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ's peace.
For all who are grieving, that God may comfort their hearts, wipe away every tear, and grant them the hope of the Resurrection.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
Hearing of your faith in the Lord Jesus
and of your love for all the holy ones,
I do not cease giving thanks for you,
remembering you in my prayers,
that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory,
may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation
resulting in knowledge of him.
May the eyes of your hearts be enlightened,
that you may know what is the hope that belongs to his call,
what are the riches of glory
in his inheritance among the holy ones,
and what is the surpassing greatness of his power
for us who believe,
in accord with the exercise of his great might,
which he worked in Christ,
raising him from the dead
and seating him at his right hand in the heavens,
far above every principality, authority, power, and dominion,
and every name that is named
not only in this age but also in the one to come.
And he put all things beneath his feet
and gave him as head over all things to the Church,
which is his Body,
the fullness of the one who fills all things in every way.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (7) You have given your Son rule over the works of your hands.
O LORD, our LORD,
how glorious is your name over all the earth!
You have exalted your majesty above the heavens.
Out of the mouths of babes and sucklings
you have fashioned praise because of your foes.
R. You have given your Son rule over the works of your hands.
When I behold your heavens, the work of your fingers,
the moon and the stars which you set in place—
What is man that you should be mindful of him,
or the son of man that you should care for him?
R. You have given your Son rule over the works of your hands.
You have made him little less than the angels,
and crowned him with glory and honor.
You have given him rule over the works of your hands,
 putting all things under his feet.
R. You have given your Son rule over the works of your hands.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to his disciples: 
 “I tell you,
everyone who acknowledges me before others
the Son of Man will acknowledge before the angels of God.
But whoever denies me before others
will be denied before the angels of God.“Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven,
but the one who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit
will not be forgiven.
When they take you before synagogues and before rulers and authorities,
do not worry about how or what your defense will be
or about what you are to say. 
For the Holy Spirit will teach you at that moment what you should say.”

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!
